criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a retry-brief test rejects a job with two major findings and a minor one, and asserts both major findings (summary, evidence, location) appear in the retry's producer brief in BOTH the seeded (tree_retry_seed) and unseeded paths, listed the same way; it fails if the builder drops one.
criteria.evidence: I ran it: reading::tests::both_retry_paths_carry_every_major_finding_in_the_same_form passed. The test builds a job with two major findings at docs/a.md:1 and docs/b.md:2 plus one minor. It asserts that seed.must_address equals retry_findings' output and that there are exactly 2 entries, each containing its severity and location, summary and evidence. It then builds producer_brief through both paths and checks that both majors are quoted in the must-address block and the minor is absent. Dropping either major breaks the len==2 assertion and the per-text assertions. briefs.rs adds a matching test that both blocks are identical.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a test calls the real jev.rs `parse_response` (not FakeJev) on a reply with no answer to the new context-prevention question and asserts the class and repeat answers still come back and the new field is empty; a malformed or out-of-list answer is stored as an error in the field and blocks nothing.
criteria.evidence: jev::tests::the_real_parser_keeps_the_required_answers_when_the_context_answer_is_missing_or_wrong passed. It calls the real parse_response with jev_questions(&[]). With the context answer missing, the call returns Ok with the class and repeat answers and no context answer. A wrong-typed answer is passed through, and a missing required answer still returns Malformed. a_missing_or_bad_context_answer_is_kept_and_blocks_nothing also passed. Through ask_jev it checks three cases: a missing answer leaves the field None, an out-of-list answer ('more-docs') and a Boolean answer are each stored as an error, and in every case the class and repeat answers are kept.

findings.evidence: The unit tests exercise retry_findings and producer_brief directly. No run_job test checks that a 'try again on <job>' request which does not qualify for a tree retry ends up with the must-address block in its committed producer brief. The wiring is a single conditional call.

summary: The change does what the retry asked for. Retry briefs now carry every blocker and major finding of the retried job's final verification, in both the seeded and the unseeded path. Both paths use the same shared formatter and the same "Findings you must address" block. Introspection records gain a planning_stopped marker and a jev.context_prevention answer drawn from the fixed list of seven outcomes. Jev's call asks the new question. The real parse_response now treats that question as optional, so a reply without it still returns the class and repeat answers. An answer that is off the list or of the wrong type is stored as an error and blocks nothing. No resolved state was added to Finding. D130 is marked accepted with the required wording, and CHANGELOG.md and docs/records.md state the choice plainly. I ran the new targeted tests and they pass: the retry-path unit test, the real-parser test, and all 24 introspection integration tests. The recorded fmt, clippy and test checks also pass. Two minor findings remain. Six files outside the deliverables list changed, but each only adds a one-line struct field the compiler requires, and all six were in the accepted plan. No end-to-end test exercises the run.rs wiring of the unseeded path.
